sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Camelot is the fabled residence of King Arthur in medieval romance. Writers tie this court to many places. Candidates span England, Wales, Cornwall and Scotland. Sites with strong Celtic ties include Caerleon and Glastonbury. Tintagel Castle near Camelford stands in Cornwall. Exeter and Cadbury in Somerset are listed among English spots. Digs at Cadbury during the 1960s proved inconclusive. The court houses the knights of the fable. Arthur leads the court until his last battle. The name marks an ideal kingdom in the romances.
